creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Measured against the pinned 0.8.0 while building the naming feature (`corpus/herdr-0.8.0/naming/`, `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 16).

`pane.rename` emits no event of any kind, and there is no `pane.renamed` topic in the schema to subscribe to. The name became visible to a watching subscriber only when a later title change happened to carry it along on `pane_updated`.

The caller is fine: `pane.rename` answers with the whole pane payload including the new label, so Muster applies its own renames from the reply the way a split applies its settled layout. **What no client can learn is somebody else's rename.** A name set from herdr's own TUI, or from a second Muster, reaches this window only when the connection next re-snapshots.

Tabs do not have this problem - `tab.rename` emits `tab_renamed` with the new label - so the ask is just for the pane half to match: emit `pane_updated` on a rename, or add a `pane.renamed` topic.

Low urgency. One person with one window renames their own panes and sees it immediately.
title: 🔌 Upstream: a pane rename is announced to nobody
